<h1>Research</h1>

:::

## Cloud-radiative feedbacks
Changes in clouds modulate warming, and are one of the most uncertain aspects of the relationship between emissions and global-mean surface temperature. Our research uses climate models to try to understand and reduce this uncertainty.

## Climate and weather extremes
Some of the greatest impacts of climate change lie in the extreme events. Our research studies temperatue and rainfall extremes in climate models.

##### Relevant Publication
Wehner, M.F., M.L. Duffy, M. Risser, C.J. Paciorek, D.A. Stone, P. Pall, 2024, On the uncertainty of long-period return values of extreme daily precipitation, Frontiers in Climate. DOI: 10.3389/fclim.2024.1343072\
<a href="https://doi.org/10.3389/fclim.2024.1343072">Link</a> 

## The tropical circulation and rainfall
The response of the tropical atmosphere to warming is very uncertain, with large intermodel spread. Our research seeks to identify sources of intermodel spread and ultimately improve future projections of the tropical climate.

##### Relevant Publications
Duffy, M.L. and P.A. O’Gorman, 2023, Intermodel spread in Walker circulation responses linked to spread in in moist stability and radiation responses, JGR Atmospheres. DOI: 10.1029/2022JD037382\

<a href="https://doi.org/10.1175/JCLI-D-19-0365.1">Link</a> 

## *Who* does the geoscience research?
Persistent biases in who does the geoscience research inhibits progress. Our research seeks to understand gender and racial diversity amongst US geoscience faculty.
